__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Prometheus data source backing every panel

title: Wallet App - Observability
description: Application, business, host and cardinality-experiment metrics for the wallet API. Built for Assignment 1: Observability.

panels.title: Request rate by endpoint
panels.description: COUNTER. rate() converts the ever-increasing counter into requests per second averaged over a 1-minute window.

panels.title: Error rate (4xx / 5xx)
panels.description: COUNTER with a label filter. 5xx spikes during the injected-error stage of the Part E experiment.

panels.title: Request latency percentiles
panels.description: HISTOGRAM. histogram_quantile() interpolates within buckets. The [5m] window means each point summarises the previous 5 minutes, so the line lags a fault by up to 5 minutes and smooths it out.

panels.title: Latency distribution (heatmap)
panels.description: HISTOGRAM buckets drawn directly. During the 500ms fault a second band appears in the upper buckets - clearer than a percentile line.

panels.title: Avg transfer processing time
panels.description: SUMMARY. The Python client's Summary exposes only _sum and _count, so an average is all it can give - hence the histogram above for p95/p99.

panels.title: In-flight requests
panels.description: GAUGE. Goes up and down; climbs while requests are slowed by the fault.

panels.title: Injected faults (experiment only)
panels.description: COUNTER. Proves the fault actually fired, rather than relying on the clock.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Resets to zero on restart - useful when checking recovery.

panels.title: Transactions per minute by type
panels.description: COUNTER. The core business signal: is money still moving? A drop here matters even when the error rate looks fine.

panels.title: Failed vs completed transfers
panels.description: COUNTER split by status label - one metric answering two questions.

panels.title: Money in system (PKR)
panels.description: GAUGE. Sum of all wallet balances. Transfers conserve it; only top-ups and cashback move it. A sudden change is a red flag.

panels.title: Registered users
panels.description: GAUGE, though it only grows here. Modelled as a gauge because it describes current state, not an accumulating event count.

panels.title: Pending transfers
panels.description: GAUGE. Incremented on entry to the transfer service, decremented in finally. If it drifts upward and never returns to 0, transfers are stuck.

panels.title: Transfer p95 amount (PKR)
panels.description: HISTOGRAM on a business quantity rather than latency. 95% of transfers are at or below this amount.

panels.title: Transfer rejections by reason (self-explored)
panels.description: COUNTER with a reason label. This is the metric explored beyond the class examples: it separates 'users are broke' from 'users mistyped a recipient', which are very different product problems.

panels.title: Auth failures by reason (self-explored)
panels.description: COUNTER. A spike in bad_password from many users can indicate a credential-stuffing attempt; unknown_email suggests a broken signup flow.

panels.title: CPU usage %
panels.description: Derived from the idle counter: everything not idle is in use.

panels.title: Memory used %
panels.description: MemAvailable is the honest number - it accounts for reclaimable cache.

panels.title: Disk usage % (root filesystem)
panels.description: Worth watching during this assignment specifically: Elasticsearch indices and Prometheus TSDB both grow on disk.

panels.title: Network traffic
panels.description: Loopback and virtual interfaces excluded so local traffic between the stack's own components doesn't dominate.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: Compare against CPU core count; sustained load above core count means work is queuing.

panels.title: demo_requests_total series count
panels.description: THE key panel for Part E.2. With a request_id label this climbs toward 100 (one series per id). Without it, the line stays flat at 1 no matter how much traffic is sent.

panels.title: Prometheus total series in memory
panels.description: Prometheus's own view of how many series it holds. Shows the real cost of the label: memory is consumed per series, not per sample.

panels.title: Part C - send money: HTTP (left) vs gRPC (right)
HTTP POST /transfers - calls/s by status code
panels.description: COUNTER from MetricsMiddleware. 201 = created (incl. idempotent replays), 404/409/422 = business or validation rejections, 429 = rate limited.

panels.title: gRPC CreateTransfer - calls/s by method and status
panels.description: COUNTER from the gRPC interceptor. OK = success, FAILED_PRECONDITION = insufficient balance, NOT_FOUND = unknown recipient, INVALID_ARGUMENT = validation, UNAUTHENTICATED = bad token, CANCELLED = the client gave up (deadline) before the server answered.

panels.title: HTTP: non-2xx share of calls (5m)
panels.description: Everything that is not 2xx, including expected business rejections (409/404/422).

panels.title: HTTP: server errors (5xx) share (5m)
panels.description: The 'our fault' error rate. Business rejections are NOT counted here.

panels.title: gRPC: non-OK share of calls (5m)
panels.description: Counterpart of the HTTP non-2xx share (OK <-> 2xx).

panels.title: gRPC: server errors share (5m)
panels.description: Counterpart of 5xx: INTERNAL, UNKNOWN, UNAVAILABLE, DATA_LOSS.

panels.title: HTTP POST /transfers - latency p50 / p95 (5m window)
panels.description: HISTOGRAM. Each point = quantile of the previous 5 minutes. Measured SERVER-side in the HTTP middleware (routing + validation + handler + response).

panels.title: gRPC CreateTransfer - latency p50 / p95 (5m window)
panels.description: HISTOGRAM. Same 5-minute window and same bucket edges as the HTTP panel so the two are comparable. Measured SERVER-side around the handler only (excludes network and protobuf (de)serialisation).

panels.title: HTTP requests in progress (all endpoints)
panels.description: GAUGE. Process-wide (not per endpoint), so it is the closest HTTP counterpart of the gRPC gauge.

panels.title: gRPC in-flight calls
panels.description: GAUGE chosen over message size: the server has a fixed pool of 10 worker threads, so in-flight calls show saturation directly; message sizes here are tiny and constant, which would tell us nothing.

panels.title: Completed transfers/s by front end (job)
panels.description: The shared service layer records this counter in BOTH processes; the job label tells them apart: wallet-app = HTTP, wallet-grpc = gRPC.

panels.title: Idempotent replays / rate-limit rejections
panels.description: COUNTERS added in Assignment 2: duplicate transfer requests answered from the stored result, and requests rejected by the rate limiter, over the selected dashboard time range. `or vector(0)` shows 0 instead of 'No data' when nothing happened. Note increase() extrapolates to the window edges, so it can read slightly above the true integer count.

panels.title: Scrape health (up)
panels.description: 1 = Prometheus scraped the target successfully on its last attempt. Confirms the gRPC service is scraped.
